title: HELIOS GitHub deployment-environment manifest (config/github/environments.json)
description: The shape scripts/github/apply-environments.ps1 reads: an object { $comment, environments: [...] }. An entry is closed - the script refuses an unknown key rather than silently ignoring a typo that would leave a protection rule unset. Only NAMES of secrets and variables appear; values are set by the owner with `gh secret set --env` / `gh variable set --env` and never live in this repository. Do not add a $schema key to the manifest itself: it is wired to this schema through .vscode/settings.json json.schemas, like the label and milestone manifests.

name.description: Matched against live environments case-insensitively. A workflow that names an environment GitHub does not have creates it with NO protection rules, so a typo here is a silently ungated deploy - which is why the name is pinned to a shape and the apply script reports what it matched.

wait_timer.description: Minutes to hold a deployment before it may run (GitHub's cap is 43200 = 30 days). 0 means no timer; the reviewer is the gate.

prevent_self_review.description: When true the person who triggered the deployment cannot approve it. Meaningful only when reviewers is non-empty.

reviewers.description: GitHub allows at most six reviewers per environment. An EMPTY list is a valid, deliberate state - an environment with no reviewer gates nothing - so the apply script says so out loud rather than treating it as configured.

secretNames.description: NAMES only. Never a value: no secret belongs in this repository.

because.description: Why this environment exists and what it gates. Required: an environment nobody can explain is one nobody can safely change.

type.description: GitHub's own two reviewer kinds. The API wants numeric ids; the apply script resolves a login or team slug to one and refuses to guess when it cannot.

name.description: A user LOGIN or a team SLUG, not a display name.

protected_branches.description: true restricts deployments to branches with protection rules. Mutually exclusive with custom_branches: GitHub rejects both at once, and this schema does too.

custom_branches.description: Branch name or wildcard patterns allowed to deploy. The character set is narrower than git's because apply-environments.ps1 PRINTS each pattern inside a single-quoted `gh api ... -f name='<pattern>'` line for the owner to paste; a quote or a space in a pattern would produce a replay command that does something other than what the report says.

branchPolicy.description: null means every branch may deploy - the GitHub default, and the one worth stating deliberately rather than reaching by omission.

envVarName.description: An environment-variable name: what GitHub accepts, and what the workflow reads.
